fixes.why:
Round 5 made these pages part of this page's proof, so this is a change that made something worse. 'Business address' sits under 'Reviews', at the moment the page admits it has none, and the footer link now reads 'Contact & business address'. A shopper burnt by fake sites takes exactly that step. What she meets:
- The Instagram browser's top bar shows 'Contact Naira Flore | Nashik Atelier & WhatsApp Support'.
- The footer of /contact, the policy, privacy and terms pages says 'Demi-fine jewellery, 18K gold coated and crafted in Nashik', straight after a bracelet sold as PVD rhodium on surgical steel.
- The delivery FAQ says '3–7 working days' against this page's 'est. 3 to 5'.
FACTS' Never list bars bare '18K gold' and 'Mumbai atelier' here, and the same claims one tap away undo that for her.
In law:
- Misdescribing a product's composition is a false representation and an unfair trade practice under the Consumer Protection Act 2019 s.2(47).
- E-Commerce Rules r.7 asks an inventory seller to keep its advertising consistent with the goods' actual characteristics and to give the country of origin, so an unchecked 'crafted in Nashik' is the origin claim the Rules most need to be right.
- Two stated delivery windows weaken the 'stated delivery schedule' that the refund duty for late delivery is measured against.
Build note 1's test renders only JewelDetailNext, CartDrawerNext and Header, so it cannot catch any of these strings.

fixes.change: Launch blocker 6, worded: 'Putting it right after delivery. The fold says what she gets for a fault (repair, replacement or store credit). It does not say how the piece gets back to us, who pays the courier, or how soon she hears back, and the live policy page and FAQ are silent on all three. Nothing covers a piece damaged in transit, a wrong piece or a missing one either, while the page says "insured" three times. E-Commerce Rules r.7 lists "cost of return shipping" among the return information an inventory seller must display, and bars refusing to take back goods that are defective or not as described. Owner, answer three things: (a) pickup or post, and who pays; (b) how many working days until she hears back; (c) for transit damage, a wrong piece or a missing one, the reporting window and the remedy. Once answered and in FACTS, the fold's second paragraph reads, for example: "Returns are for manufacturing faults only. Tell us on WhatsApp within 7 days of delivery, with photos; we reply within <n> working days, collect the piece at no cost to you, and repair or replace it or give store credit. …". The first paragraph ends: "Arrived damaged, or not the piece you ordered? Tell us on WhatsApp within <n> hours of delivery, with photos of the parcel and the piece, and we will replace it or refund you." Every number and remedy there is the owner's to set. Until answered: nothing about pickup, postage, reply times or transit damage goes on the page, and the page does not go live.' Then delete owner item 8, which this replaces.
fixes.why:
Before anything else, a shopper burnt by fake sites asks 'what if it arrives broken?'. For COD (45% of orders, FACTS) she has paid cash before she can open the parcel. 'Tell us on WhatsApp' tells her where to complain, not whether she must find a courier and pay to send jewellery to Nashik. That is the information the Rules name, and the one a dispute turns on.
The bench sets the floor she compares against: GIVA's first screen reads 'Easy 15-Day Return Policy, No Questions Asked' (bench/giva-fold-clean.png), and CaratLane lists '15-day returns, Free shipping'.
A stated free pickup may also give a COD buyer one reason fewer to refuse the parcel at the door (COD RTO 21% against about 1% prepaid, FACTS). That is a hypothesis to read in the RTO reasons, not a promise.
It is a launch blocker rather than an owner item because it is a disclosure the Rules require, not an improvement.

fixes.change: Owner item, worded: 'Cancelling before dispatch. The page says "we cannot take a piece back for a change of mind" and "COD available", and nothing about cancelling an order before it ships. The Terms say only that Naira may cancel ("NAIRA reserves the right to cancel or refuse any order"). Owner: can she cancel on WhatsApp before dispatch, at no cost, and until when? If yes, add it to FACTS. The fold's second paragraph then ends "Changed your mind before it ships? Message us on WhatsApp and we will cancel the order at no cost.", and the Questions fold adds "Can I cancel?" with the same words. If a fee would apply, E-Commerce Rules r.4 allow a cancellation charge only where Naira bears a similar charge when it cancels.' Until answered, nothing about cancelling goes on the page.
fixes.why: Read beside 'COD available', 'no change-of-mind returns' tells a COD buyer that once she has ordered, her only exit is refusing the parcel at the door. That is the costliest outcome for both sides: COD RTO is 21% against about 1% prepaid (FACTS). A stated free cancellation before dispatch gives her a cheaper exit and costs Naira nothing to say. It also answers the burnt shopper's fear of being locked into an order with a stranger. Salty puts a 'Cancellation Policy' fold on its PDP (bench/salty-text.txt). Whether it lowers RTO is a hypothesis: read cancellations against RTOs for a month.

roadmap:
Launch blockers that need ops and the owner:
- 1: measure the bracelet closed and say whether the clasp adjusts.
- 2: run one Fastrr COD checkout each to 800001 and 781001.
- 3: say what 'worn' and 'washed' mean against a fault found in week one.
- 4: choose the COD fee wording that holds on the Buy now route.
- 5: give the basis for ₹3,999 (MRP, or remove it).
- 6 (new, fix 2): pickup or post, who pays, reply time, and the transit-damage remedy.

Origin (fix 1's owner item): where Naira Petite pieces are made. If any are imported, each piece gets an Origin row with the importer's name and address, and no page says 'crafted in Nashik' of the jewellery.
Cancellation before dispatch (fix 3): the owner's rule, then one sentence in the fold and the FAQ.

Seller identity (E-Commerce Rules r.4): legal name, GSTIN, customer-care hours and a named grievance officer (acknowledge within 48 hours, resolve within a month), first in FACTS, then in a footer line on every PDP. A GSTIN she can look up is the strongest proof she can check herself.

Reviews: an app that meets IS 19000:2022. That means published collection and moderation terms, no suppression of negative reviews, 'verified' only on an order match, incentives disclosed, requests sent 7 days after delivery, and photo reviews. WhatsApp chats are never published as reviews without written consent.

Riya: her handle, whether the video was paid or gifted, and written rights for the site and ads. Then the clean 3.3 s cut with 'Creator collaboration' burned in, and a check of any running ad that uses her full reel ('Two years plating guarantee').
'Tarnish free' and 'waterproof': either substantiation on file or a real written cover window, never the invented '3-year plating assurance'.

Data protection: when the DPDP Rules' notice-and-consent duties take effect (phased in after their November 2025 notification), add a consent notice for the pixel's hashed match keys and Clarity's recordings. It must never cover the first screen, and the build-note tests should assert that.
Off-site listings: check the return-policy settings in Google Merchant Center and Meta Commerce, so catalogue ads never advertise a return window the policy does not give.
Owner decision: whether a true store-level line such as '222 orders shipped' may appear near Reviews. It stays off until approved.
A courier API with a pincode check, so the estimate becomes a dated promise only where a courier backs it.
